words.w: How does V8 run JavaScript, and why should objects keep the same shape?
words.t: V8 сначала интерпретирует, горячий код компилирует. Быстрый код ждёт одинаковую форму объектов (те же поля, тот же порядок). Иначе деоптимизация.
a: How does V8 run JavaScript, and why should objects keep the same shape
words.ex: V8 turns the code into bytecode and runs it. While it runs, it watches which types it sees. Code that runs often is compiled to fast machine code. This fast code expects objects to look the same every time: same fields, same order. If I add fields in a different order, or change a field from number to string, the fast code is thrown away. So I create objects in one place with all fields, and I do not use delete in hot code.
words.exT: V8 сначала интерпретирует, горячий код компилирует. Быстрый код ждёт одинаковую форму объектов (те же поля, тот же порядок). Иначе деоптимизация.

words.w: How does garbage collection work in V8?
words.t: Молодое поколение чистится часто и дёшево, старое — редко, инкрементально и в фоне. Даже без утечек много аллокаций даёт фризы.
a: How does garbage collection work in V8
words.ex: Most objects die very fast. So V8 keeps new objects in a small young space and cleans it often. This cleaning is cheap. Objects that survive two cleanings move to the old space. The old space is cleaned with mark and sweep. This is done in small steps and partly in background threads, so the page does not freeze. One important point: even without a leak, creating many objects very fast makes the GC work hard, and the user sees small freezes.
words.exT: Молодое поколение чистится часто и дёшево, старое — редко, инкрементально и в фоне. Даже без утечек много аллокаций даёт фризы.

words.w: What are the common memory leaks in a single-page app, and how do you find them?
words.t: Утечки: неснятые слушатели и таймеры, замыкания с большими данными, удалённые DOM-узлы в переменных, растущие кэши. Ищу сравнением heap snapshots.
a: What are the common memory leaks in a single-page app, and how do you find them
words.ex: The usual leaks are simple. An event listener or setInterval that nobody removes. A closure that keeps a big array alive. A DOM node that is removed from the page but still stored in a variable. A cache or a store that grows and never deletes anything. To find them, I open DevTools, take a heap snapshot, repeat the action several times, take another snapshot, and compare. I look at what grew and who holds it. The allocation timeline shows which code creates the objects.
words.exT: Утечки: неснятые слушатели и таймеры, замыкания с большими данными, удалённые DOM-узлы в переменных, растущие кэши. Ищу сравнением heap snapshots.

words.w: WeakMap, WeakSet, WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry — when do you use them?

a: WeakMap, WeakSet, WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry — when do you use them
words.ex: A normal Map keeps its keys alive forever. A WeakMap does not: when the key object is gone, the entry is gone too. So I use it to store extra data about an object, for example private data or a cache by object. A WeakRef is a reference that can become empty at any time. A FinalizationRegistry calls a function after an object is collected. We never know when that happens, so I use these two only for caches where losing data is fine.

words.w: structuredClone vs JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) vs spread?

a: structuredClone vs JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) vs spread
words.ex: Spread is a shallow copy. Nested objects are still shared. The JSON trick is a deep copy but with problems: undefined is removed, a Date becomes a string, Map and Set become empty objects, and a circular reference throws. structuredClone is the right tool for a deep copy. It handles Dates, Maps, Sets and cycles. But it throws on functions and DOM nodes, and class instances become plain objects.

words.w: What is the difference between the call stack, the heap and the task queues?
words.t: Стек — текущие функции (переполнение при глубокой рекурсии), куча — объекты (утечка = рост), очереди — колбэки для event loop (долгая задача = фриз).
a: What is the difference between the call stack, the heap and the task queues
words.ex: The call stack is the list of functions that are running now. If recursion goes too deep, the stack overflows. The heap is the memory where objects live; the garbage collector manages it, and a leak means the heap grows. The task queues hold callbacks, for example from setTimeout or promises. The event loop takes them one by one when the stack is empty. A long function on the stack blocks the loop, and the page freezes.
words.exT: Стек — текущие функции (переполнение при глубокой рекурсии), куча — объекты (утечка = рост), очереди — колбэки для event loop (долгая задача = фриз).

words.w: In what order do microtasks, macrotasks, requestAnimationFrame and rendering run?
words.t: Макрозадача → все микрозадачи (и новые тоже) → при кадре rAF и рендер. Бесконечные микрозадачи блокируют отрисовку; setTimeout(0) — следующий оборот.
a: In what order do microtasks, macrotasks, requestAnimationFrame and rendering run
words.ex: The event loop takes one macrotask, for example a click handler. After it, the loop runs every microtask, so all promise callbacks. If a microtask adds another microtask, it also runs now. This is why an endless promise chain freezes the page. Then, if the screen needs a new frame, the browser runs requestAnimationFrame callbacks, calculates layout and paints. setTimeout with zero delay is a new macrotask, so it runs after the paint may already have happened.
words.exT: Макрозадача → все микрозадачи (и новые тоже) → при кадре rAF и рендер. Бесконечные микрозадачи блокируют отрисовку; setTimeout(0) — следующий оборот.

words.w: What does async/await become after compilation, and how much does await cost?
words.t: Async-функция — машина состояний на промисах; await стоит один microtask; код после await всегда позже; внутри try/catch нужен return await.
a: What does async/await become after compilation, and how much does await cost
words.ex: An async function is split into steps. Each await is a point where the function stops and later continues from a promise callback. Since 2019, await on a native promise costs one microtask. Even `await 42` goes to the microtask queue. So the code after await always runs later, not right now. This matters for tests that check order, and for try/catch: inside a try block I must write `return await`, otherwise the catch does not see the error.
words.exT: Async-функция — машина состояний на промисах; await стоит один microtask; код после await всегда позже; внутри try/catch нужен return await.

words.w: How do you cancel an async operation in JavaScript?
words.t: Промисы не отменяются. AbortController: signal в fetch и свои функции, проверка между шагами, abort в cleanup эффекта. AbortSignal.timeout/any для комбинаций.
a: How do you cancel an async operation in JavaScript
words.ex: A promise has no cancel method. The standard tool is AbortController. I create a controller and pass controller.signal to fetch, to addEventListener and to my own async functions. Inside them I check signal.aborted between steps or stop when the abort event fires. In React I create the controller inside useEffect and call abort in the cleanup function. This also fixes the problem when an old request finishes after a new one. AbortSignal.timeout and AbortSignal.any help to combine a timeout with user cancel.
words.exT: Промисы не отменяются. AbortController: signal в fetch и свои функции, проверка между шагами, abort в cleanup эффекта. AbortSignal.timeout/any для комбинаций.

words.w: What is an unhandled rejection, and how do you handle errors globally in the browser?
words.t: Промис отклонён без catch → unhandledrejection; плюс window.onerror и error boundaries, отправка в мониторинг. Ошибки в хендлерах и async до boundary не доходят.
a: What is an unhandled rejection, and how do you handle errors globally in the browser
words.ex: If a promise rejects and no catch is attached before the microtask queue is empty, the browser fires the unhandledrejection event. I listen to it and to window.onerror for normal errors. I send them to a service like Sentry with the user id and the app version, and I show a simple fallback. Render errors in React go to error boundaries. But errors in event handlers and in async code do not reach boundaries, so the global handlers are the safety net.

a: Async iterators and generators — where are they useful on the frontend
words.ex: An async generator is a function that gives values one by one, and each value can arrive later. I use it to read a fetch body as a stream, to consume server-sent events, or to walk through API pages. The consumer uses for await. It asks for the next value only when it is ready, so the producer does not run ahead. To stop, I just break out of the loop. The logic is also easy to test without React.

words.w: Web Workers — what would you move there, and how?
words.t: В воркер — тяжёлые вычисления без DOM. Общение через postMessage, ArrayBuffer передавать без копии, Comlink для удобства. Service worker — другое, это сетевой прокси.
a: Web Workers — what would you move there, and how
words.ex: A worker is a second thread. It cannot touch the DOM, but it can do heavy work while the page stays smooth. Good candidates are parsing a big JSON or CSV, building a search index, compressing or resizing images. The page and the worker talk with postMessage. For big data I transfer the ArrayBuffer instead of copying it. A library like Comlink makes worker calls look like normal async functions. A service worker is different: it is a network proxy, not a place for computations.
words.exT: В воркер — тяжёлые вычисления без DOM. Общение через postMessage, ArrayBuffer передавать без копии, Comlink для удобства. Service worker — другое, это сетевой прокси.

words.w: How do you implement retry with exponential backoff correctly?
words.t: Ретраить только безопасные запросы и ретраибельные ошибки (сеть, 429, 5xx). Задержка растёт с джиттером, лимит попыток, Retry-After, стоп по signal, idempotency key для POST.
a: How do you implement retry with exponential backoff correctly
words.ex: First I check that the request is safe to repeat. A GET is safe. A POST is safe only if it has an idempotency key. Then I check the error: network errors, 429 and 5xx can be retried; 400 or 401 cannot. The delay grows, for example 1, 2, 4 seconds, with a random part so that many clients do not retry at the same moment. If the server sends a Retry-After header, I use that value. I stop after a few tries, and I also stop if the AbortSignal fires.
words.exT: Ретраить только безопасные запросы и ретраибельные ошибки (сеть, 429, 5xx). Задержка растёт с джиттером, лимит попыток, Retry-After, стоп по signal, idempotency key для POST.

words.w: setTimeout, setInterval, requestAnimationFrame, requestIdleCallback — what is the difference?
words.t: setTimeout — минимальная задержка; setInterval накапливается; rAF — перед кадром, для анимаций и измерений; rIC — в простое, для неприоритетного.
a: setTimeout, setInterval, requestAnimationFrame, requestIdleCallback — what is the difference
words.ex: setTimeout gives a minimum delay, not an exact one, and background tabs slow it down. setInterval keeps firing even if the previous callback is still slow, so I usually use setTimeout that calls itself. requestAnimationFrame runs right before the browser paints and stops in hidden tabs. It is the right place for animations and for reading layout. requestIdleCallback runs when the browser has nothing else to do, so it is good for low-priority work like analytics, and it gives a deadline I must respect.

words.w: How does fetch streaming work, and when would you use it?
words.t: response.body — ReadableStream: читаю чанки, декодирую TextDecoder, показываю сразу (стриминг ответа ИИ, большие выгрузки); отмена через signal.
a: How does fetch streaming work, and when would you use it
words.ex: Normally I call response.json() and wait for the whole body. With streaming I take response.body.getReader() and read small chunks as they come. I decode them with a TextDecoder in stream mode and show the text right away. This is how chat apps show AI answers word by word. It also lets me start rendering a big list before the download ends. The abort signal cancels the stream. When I split the text by lines, I must keep the last incomplete piece for the next chunk.

words.w: What is a closure, how does it work in memory, and where does it cause bugs?
words.t: Замыкание — функция плюс переменные вокруг неё; они живут, пока жива функция. Используется везде: приватные переменные, debounce, хуки. Баги: старые значения в колбэках, var в циклах, утечки памяти.
a: What is a closure, how does it work in memory, and where does it cause bugs
words.ex: A closure is a function plus the variables around it. When I create a function inside another function, the inner function remembers the outer variables. It keeps them even after the outer function has returned. The engine does not copy the values; it keeps the real variables alive in memory while the inner function exists. I use closures every day: a counter with a private variable, debounce, event handlers, and every React hook. The typical bugs: a callback uses an old value because it was created in an old render; a for loop with var gives the same i to every callback; and a closure that holds a big array keeps it in memory for too long.
words.exT: Замыкание — функция плюс переменные вокруг неё; они живут, пока жива функция. Используется везде: приватные переменные, debounce, хуки. Баги: старые значения в колбэках, var в циклах, утечки памяти.

words.w: How does lexical scope work, and what is the scope chain?
words.t: Область видимости определяется местом в коде, а не вызовом. Поиск переменной идёт по цепочке наружу до глобальной. Цепочка фиксируется при создании функции — отсюда замыкания. Исключение — this.
a: How does lexical scope work, and what is the scope chain
words.ex: JavaScript has lexical scope. This means the engine decides which variables a function can see by looking at where the function is written in the code. Each function creates a new scope, and blocks with let and const create block scopes. When the code reads a variable, the engine looks in the current scope first. If it is not there, it looks in the outer scope, and so on up to the global scope. This chain is fixed when the function is created, and that is exactly what makes closures possible. The only exception is this, which depends on how the function is called, not where it is written.
words.exT: Область видимости определяется местом в коде, а не вызовом. Поиск переменной идёт по цепочке наружу до глобальной. Цепочка фиксируется при создании функции — отсюда замыкания. Исключение — this.

words.w: What is the iterable protocol, and why does spread work on a Map but not on a plain object?
words.t: Итерируемое = есть Symbol.iterator, который возвращает объект с next(). Map/Set/массивы — да, объект — нет; поэтому [...obj] падает, а {...obj} работает через ключи.
a: What is the iterable protocol, and why does spread work on a Map but not on a plain object
words.ex: for-of, array spread, Array.from and destructuring all use one protocol. They call the Symbol.iterator method and then call next() until done is true. Map, Set, arrays and strings have this method. A plain object does not, so [...obj] throws. But {...obj} works, because object spread does not use the protocol; it just copies own keys. I can make my own class iterable by adding a generator method named Symbol.iterator.
words.exT: Итерируемое = есть Symbol.iterator, который возвращает объект с next(). Map/Set/массивы — да, объект — нет; поэтому [...obj] падает, а {...obj} работает через ключи.

words.w: What are Proxy and Reflect, and which libraries use them?
words.t: Proxy перехватывает операции с объектом, Reflect делает стандартное действие. На этом стоят Vue 3, MobX, Immer. Минусы — скорость и нет полифила.
a: What are Proxy and Reflect, and which libraries use them
words.ex: A Proxy sits between the code and the object. When the code reads a field, the Proxy's get trap runs; when it writes, the set trap runs. Reflect.get and Reflect.set do the normal operation, so a trap can do its work and then call the default. Vue 3 uses the get trap to remember which component read a field, and the set trap to update that component. Immer uses a Proxy to record changes and then builds a new immutable object. The cost is speed in hot code, and a Proxy cannot be polyfilled.
words.exT: Proxy перехватывает операции с объектом, Reflect делает стандартное действие. На этом стоят Vue 3, MobX, Immer. Минусы — скорость и нет полифила.

words.w: What are Symbols for, besides unique keys?
words.t: Символы — уникальные ключи, невидимые для JSON и keys; well-known символы — хуки языка (iterator, toPrimitive, hasInstance); Symbol.for — общий символ по имени.
a: What are Symbols for, besides unique keys
words.ex: A symbol is a unique key that JSON.stringify and Object.keys skip. The well-known symbols are hooks into the language. Symbol.iterator makes an object work with for-of. Symbol.toPrimitive controls what happens when the object is turned into a string or a number. Symbol.hasInstance customizes instanceof. Symbol.for('name') returns the same symbol everywhere, even across iframes. React uses it for the $$typeof field on elements, so that an element from JSON cannot be injected.
words.exT: Символы — уникальные ключи, невидимые для JSON и keys; well-known символы — хуки языка (iterator, toPrimitive, hasInstance); Symbol.for — общий символ по имени.

words.w: How do ES modules differ from CommonJS at runtime?
words.t: ESM — статическая линковка, живые привязки, асинхронно; CJS — синхронный require, копия значения. Смесь даёт default undefined; tree shaking работает только с ESM.
a: How do ES modules differ from CommonJS at runtime
words.ex: With ES modules the browser or bundler first reads all import and export statements, builds the graph and links everything. Only then the code runs. An import is a live link: if the exported value changes, the importer sees the change. Top-level await is possible. CommonJS is different: require is a normal function call that runs the file right now and returns module.exports as it is at that moment. When tools mix the two, a CommonJS module shows up as an object with a default field, and that is where "default is undefined" comes from. Tree shaking needs the static ES module graph.
words.exT: ESM — статическая линковка, живые привязки, асинхронно; CJS — синхронный require, копия значения. Смесь даёт default undefined; tree shaking работает только с ESM.

words.w: How do class fields, private fields and arrow methods work with this?
words.t: Поля создаются до тела конструктора; #private — настоящая приватность; стрелочное поле держит this, но копируется на каждый экземпляр и не переопределяется через прототип.
a: How do class fields, private fields and arrow methods work with this
words.ex: Field initializers run for every new instance, in order, before the constructor body, and this is already set. A field with # is private: no code outside the class can read it, and `#x in obj` checks if an object has it. An arrow function as a field captures this, so I can pass it as a callback safely. The price: every instance holds its own function, and a subclass cannot override it on the prototype. Normal methods are shared through the prototype and lose this when passed as callbacks.
words.exT: Поля создаются до тела конструктора; #private — настоящая приватность; стрелочное поле держит this, но копируется на каждый экземпляр и не переопределяется через прототип.

words.w: What is prototype pollution, and how do you protect against it?
words.t: Deep merge чужого JSON с ключом __proto__ меняет Object.prototype. Защита: блокировать __proto__/constructor/prototype, Map или null-прототип, обновлять библиотеки.
a: What is prototype pollution, and how do you protect against it
words.ex: Imagine a deep merge function that copies user JSON into a config object. If the JSON has a key "__proto__", the merge writes to Object.prototype. Now every object in the app has that field, for example isAdmin: true. To protect: the merge and the deep-set helpers must skip the keys __proto__, constructor and prototype. User data is better kept in a Map or in an object created with Object.create(null). And I keep libraries like lodash updated, because they had exactly this bug.
words.exT: Deep merge чужого JSON с ключом __proto__ меняет Object.prototype. Защита: блокировать __proto__/constructor/prototype, Map или null-прототип, обновлять библиотеки.

words.w: Explain property descriptors, getters and setters, and Object.freeze.
words.t: Дескрипторы: writable/enumerable/configurable или get/set. freeze поверхностный. Геттеры дали реактивность до Proxy; non-enumerable скрывает поле от JSON и spread.
a: Explain property descriptors, getters and setters, and Object.freeze
words.ex: Object.defineProperty lets me set the flags of a property. writable means it can change, enumerable means it shows up in loops and in spread, configurable means it can be deleted or changed again. A property can also be a pair of get and set functions. Object.freeze turns off writable and configurable for all own properties, but nested objects are not frozen, so a deep freeze needs recursion. Vue 2 and MobX used getters and setters to watch changes before Proxy existed. A non-enumerable property is a way to hide a helper field from JSON and spread.
words.exT: Дескрипторы: writable/enumerable/configurable или get/set. freeze поверхностный. Геттеры дали реактивность до Proxy; non-enumerable скрывает поле от JSON и spread.

words.w: Conditional types with infer — how do you get a function's return type or a promise's value?
words.t: infer — переменная типа внутри extends; так написаны ReturnType, Parameters, Awaited. Условный тип применяется к каждому члену union; обернуть в кортеж, чтобы выключить.
a: Conditional types with infer — how do you get a function's return type or a promise's value
words.ex: infer declares a type variable inside the extends check, and TypeScript finds its value. This is how ReturnType, Parameters and Awaited are written. When the type parameter is a union, TypeScript applies the conditional type to each member separately, so Unwrap<A | B> becomes Unwrap<A> | Unwrap<B>. Usually this is what I want. If not, I wrap both sides in a tuple: [T] extends [X].
words.exT: infer — переменная типа внутри extends; так написаны ReturnType, Parameters, Awaited. Условный тип применяется к каждому члену union; обернуть в кортеж, чтобы выключить.

words.w: Mapped types and template literal types — give a practical example.
words.t: Mapped type — цикл по ключам, as переименовывает/фильтрует; шаблонные литералы строят имена: onNameChange из name, типизированные параметры роута из пути.
a: Mapped types and template literal types — give a practical example
words.ex: A mapped type is a loop over keys: { [K in keyof T]: ... }. With the as clause I can change the key name or drop some keys. Template literal types build strings at the type level. Together they let me take a props type and produce an event handlers type, for example onNameChange for the field name. Another example is typed route params from a path like "/users/:id". The compiler then catches renames for free.
words.exT: Mapped type — цикл по ключам, as переименовывает/фильтрует; шаблонные литералы строят имена: onNameChange из name, типизированные параметры роута из пути.

words.w: What is structural typing, and when does it cause problems?
words.t: Типы сравниваются по форме, не по имени: UserId и OrderId как string можно перепутать. Решение — брендированные типы; проверка лишних полей только для литералов.
a: What is structural typing, and when does it cause problems
words.ex: In TypeScript, if two types have the same fields, they are compatible. This is flexible, but it has a downside: two different IDs that are both strings can be swapped and nothing complains. The fix is a branded type: type UserId = string & { __brand: 'UserId' } and a small function that creates it. Another surprise: extra properties are checked only when you write an object literal directly, not when you pass a variable.
words.exT: Типы сравниваются по форме, не по имени: UserId и OrderId как string можно перепутать. Решение — брендированные типы; проверка лишних полей только для литералов.

words.w: Why can you pass Array<Dog> where Array<Animal> is expected, and why is that unsafe?
words.t: Массивы ковариантны ради удобства, для мутабельных это небезопасно. Параметры функций проверяются наоборот (strictFunctionTypes), но не для методов.
a: Why can you pass Array<Dog> where Array<Animal> is expected, and why is that unsafe
words.ex: If Dog is an Animal, TypeScript also says Array<Dog> is an Array<Animal>. For reading this is fine. For writing it is not: through the Animal-typed reference I can push a Cat into the Dog array. TypeScript allows this on purpose, because the strict version would be very annoying. Function parameters work in the opposite direction: a function that accepts Animal can be used where a function that accepts Dog is expected. strictFunctionTypes enforces this for function types, but not for methods.
words.exT: Массивы ковариантны ради удобства, для мутабельных это небезопасно. Параметры функций проверяются наоборот (strictFunctionTypes), но не для методов.

words.w: satisfies vs a type annotation vs as const — when do you use each?
words.t: Аннотация расширяет тип; satisfies проверяет, но сохраняет точный вывод; as const сужает литералы. Для таблиц констант — as const satisfies T.
a: satisfies vs a type annotation vs as const — when do you use each
words.ex: If I write const routes: Record<string, Route> = {...}, TypeScript forgets the real keys, so routes.home is just a Route and may not exist. With satisfies Record<string, Route>, the object is checked, but its exact keys stay known. as const makes values exact: 'GET' stays the literal 'GET', arrays become readonly tuples. For tables of constants I use both together: as const satisfies T.
words.exT: Аннотация расширяет тип; satisfies проверяет, но сохраняет точный вывод; as const сужает литералы. Для таблиц констант — as const satisfies T.

words.w: How do you make a switch over a union exhaustive, and why does never help?
words.t: В default передаю значение в assertNever(x: never). Новый вариант union ломает компиляцию ровно там, где не обработан.
a: How do you make a switch over a union exhaustive, and why does never help
words.ex: I write a small helper: function assertNever(x: never): never. In the default case of the switch I call it with the value. If all cases are handled, the value's type at that point is never, so it compiles. When a new variant is added to the union and not handled, the type is no longer never, and the build fails exactly at the switch that needs a new case. This is a cheap safety net for reducers and status rendering.
words.exT: В default передаю значение в assertNever(x: never). Новый вариант union ломает компиляцию ровно там, где не обработан.

words.w: Enums vs a union of string literals vs an as const object?
words.t: Предпочитаю union литералов или as const объект: ноль рантайма, работает со всеми сборщиками. Числовые enum небезопасны, const enum ломается на границах модулей и в esbuild.
a: Enums vs a union of string literals vs an as const object
words.ex: A union of string literals is only a type, so it costs nothing at runtime. When I also need the values in code, I write an object with as const and derive the type with typeof Obj[keyof typeof Obj]. TypeScript enums generate real objects. Numeric enums accept any number, which is unsafe. const enum is inlined by tsc but not by esbuild or Babel, and it does not work across package boundaries. Many teams simply forbid enums.
words.exT: Предпочитаю union литералов или as const объект: ноль рантайма, работает со всеми сборщиками. Числовые enum небезопасны, const enum ломается на границах модулей и в esbuild.

words.w: Which strict flags matter most, and what does noUncheckedIndexedAccess change?
words.t: strict — база; noUncheckedIndexedAccess делает индекс T | undefined; exactOptionalPropertyTypes отличает отсутствие поля от undefined; verbatimModuleSyntax требует import type.
a: Which strict flags matter most, and what does noUncheckedIndexedAccess change
words.ex: strict turns on null checks, no implicit any, strict function types and a few more. noUncheckedIndexedAccess says: an index access may give undefined, so handle it. It catches real bugs in loops and lookups, but adds some noise. exactOptionalPropertyTypes makes { a?: T } different from { a: T | undefined }. verbatimModuleSyntax forces me to write import type for types, so bundlers can drop those imports without running the type checker.
words.exT: strict — база; noUncheckedIndexedAccess делает индекс T | undefined; exactOptionalPropertyTypes отличает отсутствие поля от undefined; verbatimModuleSyntax требует import type.

words.w: How do you type a generic React component, and what is the problem with forwardRef?
words.t: Дженерик-компонент — дженерик-функция, T выводится из пропсов. forwardRef теряет дженерик (нужен каст); в React 19 ref — обычный проп.
a: How do you type a generic React component, and what is the problem with forwardRef
words.ex: A generic component is just a generic function. When I write <Table rows={users} />, TypeScript infers T from the rows prop, and the render callbacks are typed. forwardRef returns a non-generic type, so the generic is lost. The old workaround was a cast or a module declaration. In React 19 function components receive ref as a normal prop, so forwardRef is not needed. For components with an as prop I use the ComponentPropsWithoutRef pattern.
words.exT: Дженерик-компонент — дженерик-функция, T выводится из пропсов. forwardRef теряет дженерик (нужен каст); в React 19 ref — обычный проп.

words.w: Where does TypeScript stop protecting you at runtime, and what do you do about it?
words.t: Типы исчезают в рантайме; сеть, storage, URL, JSON.parse — unknown. Валидирую на границе через zod/valibot и беру тип из схемы.
a: Where does TypeScript stop protecting you at runtime, and what do you do about it
words.ex: Everything that comes from outside is unknown at runtime: API responses, localStorage, query strings, messages from iframes. A cast like as User only makes the compiler quiet; it does not check anything. So I describe the data once with a zod or valibot schema, parse it at the boundary, and use z.infer to get the TypeScript type from the same schema. Then the type and the check can never disagree. In forms the same schema gives validation messages.
words.exT: Типы исчезают в рантайме; сеть, storage, URL, JSON.parse — unknown. Валидирую на границе через zod/valibot и беру тип из схемы.

words.w: What happens between setState and the change on the screen?
words.t: setState → апдейт с приоритетом → render-фаза строит новое дерево (может прерываться) → commit синхронно меняет DOM → layout-эффекты → paint → useEffect.
a: What happens between setState and the change on the screen
words.ex: When I call setState, React stores the update on that component with a priority and schedules work. In the render phase React calls the component functions, compares the result with the current tree and collects the changes. With concurrent features this phase can pause and continue later. The commit phase is synchronous: React changes the DOM, runs useLayoutEffect and ref callbacks. Then the browser paints. After that React runs useEffect callbacks. This is why render must have no side effects, and why layout effects block the paint.
words.exT: setState → апдейт с приоритетом → render-фаза строит новое дерево (может прерываться) → commit синхронно меняет DOM → layout-эффекты → paint → useEffect.

words.w: What problem does concurrent rendering solve, and what are lanes?
words.t: Конкурентный рендер прерывает тяжёлые обновления ради срочного ввода. Lanes — уровни приоритета. useTransition помечает обновление как неприоритетное; рендер должен быть чистым.
a: What problem does concurrent rendering solve, and what are lanes
words.ex: Before React 18, a big update blocked the main thread until it was done. With concurrent rendering React works for a few milliseconds, then checks if there is more urgent work, for example a key press, and handles it first. It can continue the big render later or start it again. Lanes are the priorities: user input is urgent, a transition is low priority, idle work is lowest. useTransition marks an update as low priority, so a heavy list does not delay the key press that caused it. The rule for us: render must be pure, because it may run more than once.
words.exT: Конкурентный рендер прерывает тяжёлые обновления ради срочного ввода. Lanes — уровни приоритета. useTransition помечает обновление как неприоритетное; рендер должен быть чистым.

words.w: useTransition vs useDeferredValue vs debouncing — when do you use each?
words.t: useTransition — когда сам вызываю setState; useDeferredValue — для входящего значения. Оба про рендер; сетевые запросы требуют debounce и отмены.
a: useTransition vs useDeferredValue vs debouncing — when do you use each
words.ex: With useTransition I wrap my own setState call. The input updates right away, and the heavy list updates in the background. I also get isPending to show a spinner. useDeferredValue is for a value I do not control, for example a prop: React gives me a copy that updates when it has time. Both only help with rendering cost. If the cost is network requests, I still need debounce or request cancellation. Often I use both together.
words.exT: useTransition — когда сам вызываю setState; useDeferredValue — для входящего значения. Оба про рендер; сетевые запросы требуют debounce и отмены.

words.w: Why does StrictMode run components and effects twice in development?
words.t: StrictMode дважды вызывает рендер и эффекты (setup→cleanup→setup), чтобы показать нечистый рендер и эффекты без cleanup до того, как они сломаются в конкурентном режиме.
a: Why does StrictMode run components and effects twice in development
words.ex: In development StrictMode calls each component function two times and runs each effect as setup, then cleanup, then setup again. The double render shows side effects inside render, for example an API call or a ref change. The double effect shows subscriptions and timers that have no cleanup. These bugs would also appear when React keeps state during Fast Refresh or in future features. The fix is to make effects safe to run twice, not to remove StrictMode.
words.exT: StrictMode дважды вызывает рендер и эффекты (setup→cleanup→setup), чтобы показать нечистый рендер и эффекты без cleanup до того, как они сломаются в конкурентном режиме.

words.w: How does Suspense work under the hood?
words.t: Компонент бросает промис, ближайший Suspense ловит и показывает fallback; после resolve рендер повторяется, источник данных должен отдать результат из кэша, иначе бесконечный suspend.
a: How does Suspense work under the hood
words.ex: Suspense is built on throwing. When data is not ready, the component throws a promise-like object. React goes up to the nearest Suspense, shows the fallback and waits for the promise. When it resolves, React tries to render the component again. This time the data source must return the value right away from a cache. If it starts a new request again, the component suspends forever. That is why a plain fetch inside a component does not work, and why libraries like TanStack Query or the React 19 use hook with a stable promise are needed.
words.exT: Компонент бросает промис, ближайший Suspense ловит и показывает fallback; после resolve рендер повторяется, источник данных должен отдать результат из кэша, иначе бесконечный suspend.

words.w: How does React decide to keep or recreate a component during reconciliation?
words.t: Переиспользует при том же типе и позиции (и key в списке); иначе размонтирует вместе со стейтом. Смена key сбрасывает форму; компонент внутри компонента — новый тип каждый рендер.
a: How does React decide to keep or recreate a component during reconciliation
words.ex: React compares the new tree with the old one, child by child, by position and type. This makes the algorithm fast. If the type changes, for example a div becomes a span, React removes the whole subtree and creates a new one. If the key changes, the old instance is unmounted and a new one is mounted. I use this on purpose: changing the key of a form resets it. A common bug: a component defined inside another component is a new type on every render, so its state resets every time.
words.exT: Переиспользует при том же типе и позиции (и key в списке); иначе размонтирует вместе со стейтом. Смена key сбрасывает форму; компонент внутри компонента — новый тип каждый рендер.

words.w: What is tearing, and how does useSyncExternalStore prevent it?
words.t: Tearing — в одном рендере две версии внешнего стора из-за паузы. useSyncExternalStore сравнивает снимок и форсирует синхронный рендер; его используют Redux, Zustand.
a: What is tearing, and how does useSyncExternalStore prevent it
words.ex: With concurrent rendering a render can pause in the middle. If an external store, for example Redux, changes during the pause, components rendered later read the new value while earlier ones have the old value. For one frame the UI is inconsistent. useSyncExternalStore subscribes to the store and takes a snapshot. If the snapshot changed during render, React drops the result and renders again synchronously. Redux, Zustand and routers use this hook. It also has getServerSnapshot for SSR.
words.exT: Tearing — в одном рендере две версии внешнего стора из-за паузы. useSyncExternalStore сравнивает снимок и форсирует синхронный рендер; его используют Redux, Zustand.

words.w: Why does a click inside a portal reach a React parent that is not its DOM parent?
words.t: Синтетические события всплывают по дереву React, а не DOM; портал остаётся ребёнком в React, поэтому родитель получает клики. Для click-outside нужна DOM-проверка.
a: Why does a click inside a portal reach a React parent that is not its DOM parent
words.ex: React adds one native listener per event type on the root. When an event happens, React walks its own component tree, not the DOM tree. A modal rendered with createPortal into document.body is still a child of its React parent. So the parent's onClick sees clicks inside the modal, and context also works. The downside: a "click outside" check cannot use React propagation. It must check the DOM with element.contains or use a native listener.
words.exT: Синтетические события всплывают по дереву React, а не DOM; портал остаётся ребёнком в React, поэтому родитель получает клики. Для click-outside нужна DOM-проверка.

words.w: What is automatic batching in React 18, and what does flushSync do?
words.t: React 18 батчит все обновления в одном тике (и в промисах, таймерах). flushSync форсирует синхронный коммит, например для скролла к новому элементу.
a: What is automatic batching in React 18, and what does flushSync do
words.ex: In React 17 only updates inside React event handlers were batched. Two setState calls in a setTimeout caused two renders. With createRoot, every update in the same tick is batched, no matter where it comes from. Sometimes I need the DOM updated right away, for example to scroll to a new item after adding it. Then I wrap the setState in flushSync, and React commits synchronously. It is slower, so I use it rarely. Reading state right after setState still gives the old value, with or without batching.
words.exT: React 18 батчит все обновления в одном тике (и в промисах, таймерах). flushSync форсирует синхронный коммит, например для скролла к новому элементу.

words.w: Why do effects see old props, and how do you read the latest value without re-subscribing?
words.t: Эффект помнит значения своего рендера. Чтобы подписка жила с [] и видела свежий колбэк — ref с последним значением или useEffectEvent.
a: Why do effects see old props, and how do you read the latest value without re-subscribing
words.ex: An effect's function remembers the props and state of the render that created it. If I subscribe once with an empty array and call onMessage inside, I call the version from the first render forever. If I add onMessage to the dependencies, the effect re-subscribes on every render, which may be expensive or lose events. The pattern: keep a ref, update ref.current on every render, and call ref.current inside the effect. React's useEffectEvent does the same thing officially: it gives a stable function that always sees the current values and is not a dependency.
words.exT: Эффект помнит значения своего рендера. Чтобы подписка жила с [] и видела свежий колбэк — ref с последним значением или useEffectEvent.

words.w: Callback refs vs useRef, and when do you need useImperativeHandle?
words.t: Callback ref срабатывает при появлении/удалении узла — для измерений и observers. useRef — хранилище. useImperativeHandle — маленький API (focus, scrollTo), редко.
a: Callback refs vs useRef, and when do you need useImperativeHandle
words.ex: useRef gives me a box that keeps a value between renders, but nothing happens when it changes. A callback ref is a function that React calls with the node on mount and with null on unmount. So I can start a ResizeObserver exactly when the element exists, even if it renders conditionally. useImperativeHandle lets a child expose a few methods to the parent, for example focus or scrollToRow, instead of giving the whole DOM node. I use it rarely. Data should go through props.
words.exT: Callback ref срабатывает при появлении/удалении узла — для измерений и observers. useRef — хранилище. useImperativeHandle — маленький API (focus, scrollTo), редко.

words.w: Compound components, render props, HOCs and hooks — which problem does each solve today?
words.t: Хуки — переиспользование логики; compound components — общий стейт при свободной разметке (Radix); render props — отдать рендер потребителю; HOC — почти не используются.
a: Compound components, render props, HOCs and hooks — which problem does each solve today
words.ex: Hooks replaced most higher-order components and render props for logic reuse, because they compose without extra wrappers. Compound components use context: the parent owns the state and the consumer places the parts freely. Radix and Headless UI work this way. Render props are still the cleanest way to let the consumer decide how to render something, for example a virtual list asks how to render one row. HOCs still appear for things like withAuth around a route.
words.exT: Хуки — переиспользование логики; compound components — общий стейт при свободной разметке (Radix); render props — отдать рендер потребителю; HOC — почти не используются.

words.w: What is derived state, and why is copying props into state with useEffect a bad idea?
words.t: Производное состояние считается в рендере (useMemo при необходимости), а не копируется через useEffect — лишний рендер и устаревший кадр. Сброс — через key.
a: What is derived state, and why is copying props into state with useEffect a bad idea
words.ex: If filteredItems can be computed from items and query, storing it in state is a mistake. It needs an effect, the effect runs after render, so for one frame the UI shows old data, and then there is a second render. I compute it during render, with useMemo if it is expensive. When a parent prop should reset the local state, I change the key of the component instead of writing an effect. Effects are for syncing with something outside React, not with other state.
words.exT: Производное состояние считается в рендере (useMemo при необходимости), а не копируется через useEffect — лишний рендер и устаревший кадр. Сброс — через key.

words.w: When does React.memo not help, and how do you make it work?
words.t: memo ломается от новых ссылок в пропсах (объекты, inline-функции, children). Стабилизировать ссылки, передавать примитивы или перенести стейт ниже.
a: When does React.memo not help, and how do you make it work
words.ex: React.memo compares props one by one with ===. Any prop that is a new reference breaks it: an inline style object, an inline arrow function, items.filter() in the parent, or JSX children. I can make these references stable with useMemo and useCallback. I can pass primitive values instead of objects. Or I can restructure: move the state into the component that needs it, or pass the heavy part as children from a parent that does not re-render. First I measure with the Profiler; memo everywhere is not a plan.
words.exT: memo ломается от новых ссылок в пропсах (объекты, inline-функции, children). Стабилизировать ссылки, передавать примитивы или перенести стейт ниже.

words.w: What does the React Compiler do, and what should you stop doing when it is on?
words.t: Компилятор сам мемоизирует компоненты и хуки; ручные useMemo/useCallback почти не нужны. Требует чистого кода без мутаций; нарушители пропускаются.
a: What does the React Compiler do, and what should you stop doing when it is on
words.ex: The compiler reads the component and adds memoization itself, based on which values a piece of JSX or a callback really depends on. It is like an automatic and correct useMemo everywhere. It can only do this for code that follows the rules of React: no side effects in render, no mutation of props or state, hooks called in the same order. The ESLint plugin shows violations, and the compiler skips such components. In practice I delete most manual memoization and keep the code pure.
words.exT: Компилятор сам мемоизирует компоненты и хуки; ручные useMemo/useCallback почти не нужны. Требует чистого кода без мутаций; нарушители пропускаются.

words.w: How do you design state for a big form?
words.t: Для больших форм — неконтролируемые инпуты через react-hook-form + zod: нет рендера на каждый символ, типы из схемы; Controller — для кастомных компонентов.
a: How do you design state for a big form
words.ex: Controlled inputs re-render the form on every key press. For a few fields it is fine. For fifty fields it is slow. react-hook-form registers inputs through refs, so the browser keeps the values and React renders only when needed. It connects to zod for validation, and the types come from the same schema. For custom components like a date picker I use its Controller wrapper. The form state has the same shape as the API payload, so submit is simple.
words.exT: Для больших форм — неконтролируемые инпуты через react-hook-form + zod: нет рендера на каждый символ, типы из схемы; Controller — для кастомных компонентов.

words.w: How do you stop a context from re-rendering the whole app, and when do you move to a store?
words.t: Разделять контексты по частоте изменений, мемоизировать value, сеттеры в отдельный контекст. Нет селекторов — при частых срезах переходить на Zustand/Redux.
a: How do you stop a context from re-rendering the whole app, and when do you move to a store
words.ex: Every consumer re-renders when the context value changes, and the value is often a new object each time. So I split: theme and user change rarely, cursor position or a draft change often. I wrap the value in useMemo. I put dispatch or setters in their own context, so components that only write do not re-render on reads. Context has no selectors. When I need state.cart.count without re-rendering on state.filters, I move to Zustand or Redux, where a selector subscribes to one slice.
words.exT: Разделять контексты по частоте изменений, мемоизировать value, сеттеры в отдельный контекст. Нет селекторов — при частых срезах переходить на Zustand/Redux.

words.w: Server state vs client state — why treat them differently?
words.t: Серверное состояние — общее, асинхронное, устаревает; его ведёт query-кэш (TanStack/RTK Query). Клиентское — модалки, вкладки, формы — useState, URL, маленький стор.
a: Server state vs client state — why treat them differently
words.ex: Data from an API has a life cycle: loading, error, fresh or stale, refetch, invalidation, pagination. Writing all this by hand in Redux gives a lot of boilerplate. A query library like TanStack Query or RTK Query does it with keys, staleTime, retries and background refetch. Real client state is small: is the modal open, which tab is selected, what the user typed in a form. For that, useState, URL params or a small store are enough. Mixing the two is the most common architecture problem I see.
words.exT: Серверное состояние — общее, асинхронное, устаревает; его ведёт query-кэш (TanStack/RTK Query). Клиентское — модалки, вкладки, формы — useState, URL, маленький стор.

words.w: How do you implement optimistic updates safely?
words.t: onMutate: отменить refetch, снимок кэша, записать ожидаемое; onError — откат; onSettled — invalidate. Только для надёжных действий, не для платежей; idempotency key.
a: How do you implement optimistic updates safely
words.ex: In TanStack Query the pattern is onMutate: cancel refetches for this key, save the current data, and write the new value into the cache. onError puts the saved data back and shows a message. onSettled invalidates the query, so the real server response fixes any difference. I do this only for actions that almost always succeed and have a clear UI, like a like button. Never for payments. If the mutation can be retried, I add an idempotency key.
words.exT: onMutate: отменить refetch, снимок кэша, записать ожидаемое; onError — откат; onSettled — invalidate. Только для надёжных действий, не для платежей; idempotency key.

words.w: How do you avoid request waterfalls and race conditions when fetching data?
words.t: Водопады — фетчить параллельно и на уровне роута; гонки — abort предыдущего запроса в cleanup или сравнение id запроса. Query-библиотеки делают это по ключу.
a: How do you avoid request waterfalls and race conditions when fetching data
words.ex: A waterfall happens when a child starts its request only after the parent's data arrives. The fix is to start requests together: Promise.all, parallel queries, or a route loader that fetches before the page renders. A race condition is when an old response arrives after a new one and overwrites it. The fix is to abort the previous request in the effect cleanup, or to compare a request id before setting state. Query libraries do both: they deduplicate by key and keep only the latest result.
words.exT: Водопады — фетчить параллельно и на уровне роута; гонки — abort предыдущего запроса в cleanup или сравнение id запроса. Query-библиотеки делают это по ключу.

words.w: When do you refetch, invalidate or update the cache by hand?
words.t: Инвалидация списков после мутаций; прямое обновление кэша, когда мутация возвращает сущность; большой staleTime для справочников; refetch on focus для общих данных.
a: When do you refetch, invalidate or update the cache by hand
words.ex: I start from the nature of the data. Reference data like countries gets a long staleTime. After I create or delete an item, I invalidate the list queries so pagination stays correct. After an edit, I write the returned entity into the detail cache and patch the item in the list, so the user does not see a flash. Refetch on window focus is on for dashboards that other people edit and off for forms. The goal: the user never sees data older than acceptable, and we do not send useless requests.
words.exT: Инвалидация списков после мутаций; прямое обновление кэша, когда мутация возвращает сущность; большой staleTime для справочников; refetch on focus для общих данных.

words.w: How does Zustand avoid re-renders, and how is it different from Redux?
words.t: Zustand: стор вне React, подписка селектором, рендер только при смене среза. Redux — то же через useSelector плюс редьюсеры, действия, middleware, devtools.
a: How does Zustand avoid re-renders, and how is it different from Redux
words.ex: Zustand's store is a plain object with a subscribe function. When I write useStore(s => s.count), the component re-renders only when count changes. There is no provider and no action types. Redux Toolkit uses the same selector idea, but adds structure: immutable reducers through Immer, serializable actions, time travel in devtools, middleware, and RTK Query. I choose Zustand for UI state in an app, and Redux Toolkit when the team wants strict structure or already uses it.
words.exT: Zustand: стор вне React, подписка селектором, рендер только при смене среза. Redux — то же через useSelector плюс редьюсеры, действия, middleware, devtools.

words.w: What belongs in the URL, and how do you keep it in sync?
words.t: В URL — фильтры, пагинация, выбранный элемент, вкладка; парсить схемой с дефолтами, писать через роутер, replace + debounce для частых изменений.
a: What belongs in the URL, and how do you keep it in sync
words.ex: If the user presses refresh and loses the filters, that is a bug. I keep filters, sort, page, the selected entity and the open tab in search params. I parse them with a zod schema that has defaults, and I write them back through the router. For a search input I use replace instead of push and a debounce, so the history does not fill up. The URL becomes the single source of truth, and the state can be shared and tested.
words.exT: В URL — фильтры, пагинация, выбранный элемент, вкладка; парсить схемой с дефолтами, писать через роутер, replace + debounce для частых изменений.

words.w: How do you build infinite scroll with cursor pagination correctly?
words.t: useInfiniteQuery с курсором, sentinel через IntersectionObserver, виртуализация, стабильные ключи; новые элементы сверху — отдельный поток с коррекцией scrollTop.
a: How do you build infinite scroll with cursor pagination correctly
words.ex: The server returns items and a nextCursor. A cursor is better than an offset, because the data may change while the user scrolls. I put an empty element at the end of the list and watch it with IntersectionObserver. When it becomes visible, I call fetchNextPage, with a hasNextPage check so I do not fetch twice. For thousands of rows I virtualize, so the DOM stays small. New items at the top are different: adding them moves everything down, so I must fix scrollTop after the insert.
words.exT: useInfiniteQuery с курсором, sentinel через IntersectionObserver, виртуализация, стабильные ключи; новые элементы сверху — отдельный поток с коррекцией scrollTop.

words.w: Where is the server/client boundary in React Server Components, and what can cross it?
words.t: 'use client' начинает клиентское поддерево; пропсы через границу — только сериализуемые (JSX как children можно, функции нет), кроме server actions.
a: Where is the server/client boundary in React Server Components, and what can cross it
words.ex: In the App Router every component is a server component by default. It can read the database directly and its code is never sent to the browser. 'use client' marks the start of an interactive part. Props that cross this border must be serializable: plain objects, arrays, strings, and JSX from the server as children. Functions, class instances and Dates do not pass, with one exception: server actions, which become RPC calls. A client component cannot import a server component; it can only receive it as a prop.
words.exT: 'use client' начинает клиентское поддерево; пропсы через границу — только сериализуемые (JSX как children можно, функции нет), кроме server actions.

words.w: Explain the Next.js caching layers and how you invalidate them.
words.t: Четыре слоя: мемоизация в запросе, Data Cache между запросами, Full Route Cache для статики, Router Cache в браузере. Инвалидация — revalidatePath/Tag, no-store.
a: Explain the Next.js caching layers and how you invalidate them
words.ex: Inside one request, the same fetch call is done only once. Between requests, the Data Cache keeps fetch results until the revalidate time passes or until I call revalidateTag, for example from a server action or a webhook. If all data on a page is cacheable, the page becomes static HTML in the Full Route Cache. In the browser, the Router Cache keeps visited segments for fast back navigation. When data looks old, I check which of the four layers served it. Since Next 15, fetch is not cached by default, which removes many surprises.
words.exT: Четыре слоя: мемоизация в запросе, Data Cache между запросами, Full Route Cache для статики, Router Cache в браузере. Инвалидация — revalidatePath/Tag, no-store.

words.w: What causes hydration mismatches, and how do you fix them?
words.t: Сервер и клиент дали разное: Date.now, window, локаль, расширения, невалидная вложенность. Лечить переносом в useEffect, флагом mounted, dynamic ssr:false; suppress — крайняя мера.
a: What causes hydration mismatches, and how do you fix them
words.ex: Hydration connects React to the HTML from the server and expects the same tree. If anything differs, React warns and may re-render from scratch. Common causes: text that depends on the current time, code that renders differently when window exists, date formatting that depends on the user's locale, a div inside a p that the browser moved, or an extension that changed the page. The fix: render a neutral placeholder on the server and update it in useEffect, use a mounted flag for browser-only widgets, and keep the locale the same on both sides. suppressHydrationWarning is only for a single text node like a timestamp.
words.exT: Сервер и клиент дали разное: Date.now, window, локаль, расширения, невалидная вложенность. Лечить переносом в useEffect, флагом mounted, dynamic ssr:false; suppress — крайняя мера.

words.w: What does streaming SSR with Suspense change for the user and for the architecture?
words.t: Сервер сразу отдаёт оболочку с fallback-ами, медленные части достримливает. Лучше TTFB/LCP; нужно изолировать медленные данные в Suspense и держать размеры fallback.
a: What does streaming SSR with Suspense change for the user and for the architecture
words.ex: Without streaming the server waits for the slowest query before sending anything. With streaming it sends the layout and the fallbacks right away, keeps the connection open, and sends the HTML of each block when its data is ready, with a small script that puts it in place. The user sees the page sooner, and the LCP metric improves. For this to work, I wrap each independent data block in its own Suspense and give the fallback the right size, so the layout does not jump.
words.exT: Сервер сразу отдаёт оболочку с fallback-ами, медленные части достримливает. Лучше TTFB/LCP; нужно изолировать медленные данные в Suspense и держать размеры fallback.

words.w: How do server actions work, and what are the security risks?
words.t: 'use server' → POST-эндпоинт. Это публичный API: внутри проверять сессию и права, валидировать вход схемой, не доверять скрытым полям.
a: How do server actions work, and what are the security risks
words.ex: On the client, a server action is replaced by a reference. Calling it sends a POST request with the arguments to Next, and the function runs on the server. It works with forms and useActionState even before JavaScript loads. Security-wise, a server action is a public API. So inside it I check the session again, check that this user may change this specific resource, validate the input with a schema, and never trust a hidden id from the form. Values captured by closures are encrypted, but I still do not put secrets there.
words.exT: 'use server' → POST-эндпоинт. Это публичный API: внутри проверять сессию и права, валидировать вход схемой, не доверять скрытым полям.

words.w: Edge runtime vs Node runtime — what can you do at the edge?
words.t: Edge — быстрый старт рядом с пользователем, только Web API, без Node-модулей: редиректы, auth, A/B, заголовки. База и тяжёлое — в Node runtime.
a: Edge runtime vs Node runtime — what can you do at the edge
words.ex: Edge functions run in many regions, so they are close to the user and start in milliseconds. This makes them good for small decisions before the request reaches the app: read a cookie, redirect a user who is not logged in, choose a language, set headers. The runtime is limited: fetch, Request, Response and crypto exist, but Node built-ins do not, and the CPU time is short. Anything that needs a database driver, an ORM or heavy computation runs in the Node runtime.
words.exT: Edge — быстрый старт рядом с пользователем, только Web API, без Node-модулей: редиректы, auth, A/B, заголовки. База и тяжёлое — в Node runtime.

words.w: How does the browser use layers, and why do transform and opacity animate smoothly?
words.t: Слои двигает GPU; transform/opacity меняют только композицию, без layout и paint. will-change заранее создаёт слой, но слоёв не должно быть много.
a: How does the browser use layers, and why do transform and opacity animate smoothly
words.ex: After painting, the browser splits the page into layers and the GPU puts them together. If I animate transform or opacity on an element with its own layer, only the compositing step changes. The main thread is free and the animation stays at 60 frames per second. If I animate width or top, the browser must calculate layout and paint again for the whole affected area. will-change creates a layer in advance, but too many layers use a lot of memory. The Layers panel in DevTools shows what is being repainted.
words.exT: Слои двигает GPU; transform/opacity меняют только композицию, без layout и paint. will-change заранее создаёт слой, но слоёв не должно быть много.

words.w: preload, prefetch, preconnect, dns-prefetch, modulepreload — what does each do?
words.t: preload — критичный ресурс этой страницы; prefetch — для следующей, в простое; preconnect — соединение заранее; modulepreload — для ESM с парсингом.
a: preload, prefetch, preconnect, dns-prefetch, modulepreload — what does each do
words.ex: preload tells the browser about a resource it would find late, for example a font or the hero image. It must be used on the page, or the download is wasted. prefetch is a hint for the next navigation, done when the browser is idle. preconnect does the DNS lookup and the TLS handshake for another domain in advance; dns-prefetch does only the DNS part. modulepreload is preload for ES modules, and it also parses them. The fetchpriority attribute changes the order of downloads even more.
words.exT: preload — критичный ресурс этой страницы; prefetch — для следующей, в простое; preconnect — соединение заранее; modulepreload — для ESM с парсингом.

words.w: How do Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified and immutable work together?
words.t: max-age — свежесть; потом условный запрос по ETag → 304. Хэшированные бандлы — год + immutable; HTML — no-cache (всегда проверка); stale-while-revalidate для плавности.
a: How do Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified and immutable work together
words.ex: While the response is fresh, the browser uses the cache without any request. When it expires, the browser sends a conditional request with the ETag or the date, and the server answers 304 Not Modified, which is cheap. For bundles with a hash in the file name I set max-age of one year and immutable, because the URL changes on every deploy. For HTML I set no-cache: it is still stored, but the browser always checks with the server, so a deploy is visible right away. stale-while-revalidate shows the old version while the new one downloads in the background.
words.exT: max-age — свежесть; потом условный запрос по ETag → 304. Хэшированные бандлы — год + immutable; HTML — no-cache (всегда проверка); stale-while-revalidate для плавности.

words.w: What do you use service workers for, and what cache strategies do you combine?
words.t: Прокси в браузере: precache оболочки, cache-first для хэшированных файлов, SWR для картинок, network-first для API. Сложное — обновление воркера и не кэшировать приватный HTML.
a: What do you use service workers for, and what cache strategies do you combine
words.ex: A service worker sits between the page and the network. It can answer a request from the cache, from the network, or both. With Workbox I precache the app shell at install time. Static files with hashes are served cache-first. Images use stale-while-revalidate. API calls use network-first with a cache fallback. The hard parts are updates and privacy. A new worker waits until all tabs are closed unless I call skipWaiting and tell the user. And I must never cache a page with private data by accident.
words.exT: Прокси в браузере: precache оболочки, cache-first для хэшированных файлов, SWR для картинок, network-first для API. Сложное — обновление воркера и не кэшировать приватный HTML.

words.w: Explain the CORS preflight. When does it happen, and how do you avoid it?
words.t: Preflight OPTIONS — для non-simple запросов (JSON, Authorization, PUT/DELETE). Сервер отвечает Allow-*; с credentials нельзя *. Max-Age кэширует; BFF убирает CORS вовсе.
a: Explain the CORS preflight. When does it happen, and how do you avoid it
words.ex: A simple request, like a GET or a form POST, goes directly, and the browser only checks the response headers. If the request has an Authorization header, a JSON content type, or a method like PUT, the browser first sends OPTIONS to ask for permission. This costs one extra round trip. The server must return the allowed origin, methods and headers. If cookies are used, it must also return Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, and then the origin cannot be a star. Access-Control-Max-Age caches the preflight. A proxy on the same origin, or a BFF, removes CORS completely.
words.exT: Preflight OPTIONS — для non-simple запросов (JSON, Authorization, PUT/DELETE). Сервер отвечает Allow-*; с credentials нельзя *. Max-Age кэширует; BFF убирает CORS вовсе.

words.w: Cookie flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain — what matters for auth?
words.t: HttpOnly — не читает JS; Secure — только HTTPS; SameSite Lax блокирует CSRF, но пускает переходы по ссылке; разные домены → None + Secure + CSRF-токен.
a: Cookie flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain — what matters for auth
words.ex: For a session cookie I set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite. HttpOnly means that even if a script is injected, it cannot read the cookie. Secure means the cookie is sent only over HTTPS. SameSite=Lax means the cookie is not sent with cross-site POST requests, which blocks most CSRF, but it is sent when the user clicks a link to my site. Strict blocks even that, so a login link from an email opens a logged-out page. If the frontend and the API are on different domains, I need SameSite=None with Secure, CORS with credentials, and a CSRF token. Browsers now also partition third-party cookies by top site.
words.exT: HttpOnly — не читает JS; Secure — только HTTPS; SameSite Lax блокирует CSRF, но пускает переходы по ссылке; разные домены → None + Secure + CSRF-токен.

words.w: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events vs long polling — how do you choose?
words.t: SSE — поток сервер→клиент по HTTP с автопереподключением (уведомления, стриминг). WebSocket — двусторонний и быстрый (чат, коллаборация), но реконнект и heartbeats на мне.
a: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events vs long polling — how do you choose
words.ex: Server-sent events are a normal HTTP response that stays open. The browser reconnects automatically and sends the last event id. It works through proxies and with HTTP/2. It is perfect for notifications and for streaming AI text. WebSockets open a two-way connection. They are right when the client also sends many messages: chat, collaborative editing, games. But I must handle reconnect, heartbeats and back-pressure myself. Long polling is the fallback when the infrastructure blocks everything else.
words.exT: SSE — поток сервер→клиент по HTTP с автопереподключением (уведомления, стриминг). WebSocket — двусторонний и быстрый (чат, коллаборация), но реконнект и heartbeats на мне.

words.w: What are Intersection, Resize and Mutation Observers, and what do they replace?
words.t: IntersectionObserver — видимость (lazy load, бесконечный скролл), ResizeObserver — размер элемента, MutationObserver — изменения DOM; все асинхронные, без layout на каждом событии.
a: What are Intersection, Resize and Mutation Observers, and what do they replace
words.ex: IntersectionObserver tells me when an element enters or leaves the viewport, without reading layout on every scroll event. It makes lazy loading and infinite scroll cheap. ResizeObserver tells me when the size of an element changes, which is how container-aware components work. MutationObserver tells me about DOM changes in batches, useful with third-party widgets. All three run asynchronously, so they do not cause layout thrashing.
words.exT: IntersectionObserver — видимость (lazy load, бесконечный скролл), ResizeObserver — размер элемента, MutationObserver — изменения DOM; все асинхронные, без layout на каждом событии.

words.w: What do HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 change for bundling decisions?
words.t: HTTP/2 мультиплексирует — много мелких чанков выгодно для кэша; шардинг и спрайты не нужны. HTTP/3 на QUIC лучше на плохих сетях. Байты и парсинг JS всё равно главное.
a: What do HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 change for bundling decisions
words.ex: With HTTP/1.1 the browser opened about six connections per domain, so we merged files into one big bundle. HTTP/2 sends many streams over one connection, so splitting the bundle into cacheable chunks is good: a small change does not invalidate everything. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC on UDP, so one lost packet does not block the other streams, which helps a lot on mobile. But bytes are still not free: the browser must download, parse and run the JavaScript.
words.exT: HTTP/2 мультиплексирует — много мелких чанков выгодно для кэша; шардинг и спрайты не нужны. HTTP/3 на QUIC лучше на плохих сетях. Байты и парсинг JS всё равно главное.

words.w: How do you find why a React page is slow, step by step?
words.t: Воспроизвести с троттлингом → Performance (long tasks) → React Profiler (кто и почему рендерится) → сеть (водопады, размеры) → чинить самое крупное и перемерять.
a: How do you find why a React page is slow, step by step
words.ex: First I reproduce the problem with CPU throttling and a slow network, like a real mid-range phone. The Performance panel shows where the time goes: scripting, layout or network, and marks long tasks over 50 milliseconds. If the problem is rendering, the React Profiler shows which components rendered, how many times and why. Often the cause is state high in the tree. If the problem is network, I look for waterfalls and large responses. I fix one thing, measure again, and keep a Lighthouse or Web Vitals number as the check against regressions.
words.exT: Воспроизвести с троттлингом → Performance (long tasks) → React Profiler (кто и почему рендерится) → сеть (водопады, размеры) → чинить самое крупное и перемерять.

words.w: What is INP, and what usually makes it bad?
words.t: INP — задержка от действия до следующего кадра за весь визит. Причины: долгие обработчики, тяжёлые коммиты, синхронные чтения layout, сторонние скрипты. Лечить yield, startTransition, виртуализацией.
a: What is INP, and what usually makes it bad
words.ex: INP replaced FID. It measures almost the worst interaction during the whole page life, not just the first one. A bad INP usually means that a click handler does too much work at once, or a state change re-renders a huge tree, or code reads layout right after changing the DOM. The fixes: break long work into pieces with scheduler.yield or setTimeout, move non-urgent updates into startTransition, virtualize long lists, and move third-party scripts to a worker with Partytown.
words.exT: INP — задержка от действия до следующего кадра за весь визит. Причины: долгие обработчики, тяжёлые коммиты, синхронные чтения layout, сторонние скрипты. Лечить yield, startTransition, виртуализацией.

words.w: How do you split the code, and what stays in the main bundle?
words.t: Делить по роутам и тяжёлым редким фичам (редактор, графики, карты); оболочку держать вместе; vendor-чанк для кэша; префетч по hover/idle; не дробить слишком мелко.
a: How do you split the code, and what stays in the main bundle
words.ex: Route-based splitting with React.lazy or the framework's loader is the base. Then I split big libraries that are not needed at the start: a rich text editor, a chart library, a PDF viewer. A separate vendor chunk for stable dependencies helps caching. Too many small chunks create request chains and duplicated code, so I check the bundle analyzer and the network waterfall. Prefetching a chunk on hover or with requestIdleCallback hides the loading delay.
words.exT: Делить по роутам и тяжёлым редким фичам (редактор, графики, карты); оболочку держать вместе; vendor-чанк для кэша; префетч по hover/idle; не дробить слишком мелко.

words.w: How do you optimize images and fonts for Core Web Vitals?
words.t: Главная картинка — preload и fetchpriority high, остальное lazy; srcset/sizes, AVIF/WebP, width/height против CLS. Шрифты self-host woff2, preload, font-display и подгонка fallback.
a: How do you optimize images and fonts for Core Web Vitals
words.ex: The main image is usually the LCP element, so I give it fetchpriority="high" and a preload. Everything below the fold gets loading="lazy". srcset and sizes give each screen the right resolution, and AVIF or WebP cuts the size in half. Width and height attributes reserve space, so nothing jumps when the image loads. For fonts I host woff2 files myself, preload the main one, use only a few weights, and tune the fallback font metrics with size-adjust, so the text does not jump when the real font arrives.
words.exT: Главная картинка — preload и fetchpriority high, остальное lazy; srcset/sizes, AVIF/WebP, width/height против CLS. Шрифты self-host woff2, preload, font-display и подгонка fallback.

words.w: When is memoization harmful, and how do you decide?
words.t: Мемоизация стоит памяти и сравнений, ошибочные deps дают баги. Применять по профилю: дорогие вычисления или стабильная ссылка для memo-ребёнка. С React Compiler — автоматически.
a: When is memoization harmful, and how do you decide
words.ex: Memoization is not free. React stores the previous value, compares the dependencies on every render, and the code becomes harder to read. For cheap computations it costs more than it saves. I add it when the Profiler shows a real cost, or when a memoized child or an effect needs a stable reference. With the React Compiler the picture changes, because memoization becomes automatic and correct.
words.exT: Мемоизация стоит памяти и сравнений, ошибочные deps дают баги. Применять по профилю: дорогие вычисления или стабильная ссылка для memo-ребёнка. С React Compiler — автоматически.

words.w: How do you find and fix layout thrashing?
words.t: Чередование чтений (offsetHeight) и записей форсирует reflow на каждом шаге. Сначала все чтения, потом записи; rAF, ResizeObserver, CSS вместо измерений в JS.
a: How do you find and fix layout thrashing
words.ex: When I change a style and then read a layout property, the browser must calculate the layout right now to give the correct answer. If I do this in a loop over 100 elements, that is 100 layout calculations. In the Performance panel they appear as purple Layout blocks with a "forced reflow" warning. The fix: first read all values, then do all writes. ResizeObserver can replace manual measuring, requestAnimationFrame can group the writes, and often CSS can do the job without JavaScript.
words.exT: Чередование чтений (offsetHeight) и записей форсирует reflow на каждом шаге. Сначала все чтения, потом записи; rAF, ResizeObserver, CSS вместо измерений в JS.

words.w: Virtualization vs pagination — what are the trade-offs?
words.t: Виртуализация держит DOM маленьким, но усложняет a11y, поиск по странице, переменную высоту. Пагинация проще и лучше для SEO. Ленты — infinite query + виртуализация.
a: Virtualization vs pagination — what are the trade-offs
words.ex: With a few thousand rows the DOM itself becomes slow. Virtualization renders only the rows in view plus a small buffer, positioned absolutely inside a container with the full height. The costs: rows with different heights must be measured, screen readers lose context, Ctrl+F does not find hidden rows, and scroll restoration is harder. For tables that users scan, normal pagination is often better and cheaper. Feeds get infinite query, and virtualization when they grow.
words.exT: Виртуализация держит DOM маленьким, но усложняет a11y, поиск по странице, переменную высоту. Пагинация проще и лучше для SEO. Ленты — infinite query + виртуализация.

words.w: What is a stacking context, what creates one, and why does z-index sometimes not work?
words.t: Контекст наложения создают position+z-index, transform, opacity<1, filter, isolation. z-index сравнивается только внутри контекста. Выпадашки — через портал и шкалу z-index.
a: What is a stacking context, what creates one, and why does z-index sometimes not work
words.ex: z-index is not global. An element with position and a z-index, or with transform, opacity below one, filter, or isolation: isolate, creates its own stacking context. All its children are layered inside it. So a child with z-index 9999 cannot go above a sibling of its parent if the parent's context is below. When a dropdown is hidden behind a header, I look at the ancestors to find the context. The reliable fix is a portal to body plus a small documented scale of z-index values.
words.exT: Контекст наложения создают position+z-index, transform, opacity<1, filter, isolation. z-index сравнивается только внутри контекста. Выпадашки — через портал и шкалу z-index.

words.w: What is the containing block? Why does height: 100% often do nothing, and why does position: fixed sometimes scroll?
words.t: Абсолют — от ближайшего позиционированного предка; проценты — от containing block; transform/filter на предке превращает fixed в absolute относительно него.
a: What is the containing block? Why does height: 100% often do nothing, and why does position: fixed sometimes scroll
words.ex: For an absolutely positioned element, the containing block is the nearest ancestor with a position other than static. For a normal element it is the nearest block container. For a fixed element it is the viewport. But if an ancestor has transform, filter, perspective or contain, it becomes the containing block, and the fixed element scrolls with it. A percentage height needs a defined height on the containing block, so height: 100% does nothing until every parent in the chain has a height.
words.exT: Абсолют — от ближайшего позиционированного предка; проценты — от containing block; transform/filter на предке превращает fixed в absolute относительно него.

words.w: Container queries, cascade layers and :has — how do they change your CSS?
words.t: Container queries — стиль по ширине контейнера, не окна; @layer упорядочивает слои без войны специфичности; :has — стиль по потомкам без JS.
a: Container queries, cascade layers and :has — how do they change your CSS
words.ex: Container queries let a card change its layout when its container is narrow, no matter how wide the window is. This is what design systems always needed. Cascade layers let me order resets, framework styles, components and utilities, so a utility class always wins without !important. This is how Tailwind and design systems avoid specificity wars. With :has I can style a form field when its input is invalid, or a card that contains an image. All three are supported in all modern browsers.
