words.exT: Container queries — стиль по ширине контейнера, не окна; @layer упорядочивает слои без войны специфичности; :has — стиль по потомкам без JS.

words.w: CSS custom properties vs Sass variables vs runtime CSS-in-JS — what is the modern setup?
words.t: Токены — CSS-переменные (живые, тематизируемые). Sass — статика на сборке. Runtime CSS-in-JS тормозит и не работает в RSC; тренд — zero-runtime (vanilla-extract, Panda, Tailwind).
a: CSS custom properties vs Sass variables vs runtime CSS-in-JS — what is the modern setup
words.ex: Design tokens are best as CSS custom properties. They cascade, they can change per theme or per component, and JavaScript can read them with getComputedStyle. Sass variables are static; they are fine for math at build time. Runtime CSS-in-JS like styled-components injects styles during render, which costs performance and does not work in React Server Components. So the ecosystem moved to compile-time tools: vanilla-extract, Panda CSS, Tailwind. Same developer experience, no runtime cost.
words.exT: Токены — CSS-переменные (живые, тематизируемые). Sass — статика на сборке. Runtime CSS-in-JS тормозит и не работает в RSC; тренд — zero-runtime (vanilla-extract, Panda, Tailwind).

words.w: How do you build a fast and accessible animation?
words.t: Только transform/opacity, will-change дозированно, prefers-reduced-motion обязательно, 150–300 мс. WAAPI — контроль и промисы, View Transitions — переходы между состояниями.
a: How do you build a fast and accessible animation
words.ex: Transform and opacity are handled by the compositor, so the animation stays smooth even when the main thread is busy. I do not animate height or layout properties. For expand and collapse I use grid-template-rows or measure once and animate transform. prefers-reduced-motion must turn motion off or make it shorter for users who need it. The Web Animations API gives me promises and play, pause and reverse. The View Transitions API animates between two states of the page with very little code.
words.exT: Только transform/opacity, will-change дозированно, prefers-reduced-motion обязательно, 150–300 мс. WAAPI — контроль и промисы, View Transitions — переходы между состояниями.

words.w: Logical properties and modern layout — how do you support RTL and responsive design without many media queries?
words.t: Логические свойства (inline/block) дают RTL бесплатно; clamp() — плавная типографика; grid auto-fit/minmax и flex-wrap — адаптив без брейкпоинтов.
a: Logical properties and modern layout — how do you support RTL and responsive design without many media queries
words.ex: Logical properties replace left and right with start and end, so Arabic and Hebrew layouts flip for free. clamp() gives a font size that grows smoothly between a minimum and a maximum. grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr)) builds a responsive card grid in one line. aspect-ratio, gap and fit-content remove many wrapper divs. Media queries are then needed only for real layout changes, not for every width.
words.exT: Логические свойства (inline/block) дают RTL бесплатно; clamp() — плавная типографика; grid auto-fit/minmax и flex-wrap — адаптив без брейкпоинтов.

words.w: How do you organize a large frontend codebase so it stays maintainable?
words.t: Структура по фичам, слои с направлением зависимостей (shared→entities→features→pages), линт на импорты, публичный API модуля через index, тесты рядом.
a: How do you organize a large frontend codebase so it stays maintainable
words.ex: Folders like components, hooks and utils do not scale, because every feature touches all of them. I group code by feature, with layers, and allow imports only downward. A lint plugin like eslint-plugin-boundaries or the Feature-Sliced Design rules enforce this. Each feature exports a small public API, so I can refactor inside without breaking others. Shared UI lives in a design system package. Tests and styles live next to the code. This makes ownership clear and code splitting natural.
words.exT: Структура по фичам, слои с направлением зависимостей (shared→entities→features→pages), линт на импорты, публичный API модуля через index, тесты рядом.

words.w: Micro-frontends: when are they worth it, and how would you integrate them?
words.t: Оправданы, когда независимые команды нуждаются в независимых деплоях. Интеграция: Module Federation/import maps, общая дизайн-система и auth, изолированные стейт и стили. Часто монорепо лучше.
a: Micro-frontends: when are they worth it, and how would you integrate them
words.ex: Micro-frontends solve a team problem, not a technical one: several teams want to ship on their own schedule. The price is high: duplicated dependencies, inconsistent UX, hard routing between apps, and slower pages. If I do it, I use Module Federation or native import maps with a shell app, share React and the design system as singletons, communicate through the URL and a small event contract, and keep CSS scoped. For one team or a few teams, a monorepo with separate packages is usually the better choice.
words.exT: Оправданы, когда независимые команды нуждаются в независимых деплоях. Интеграция: Module Federation/import maps, общая дизайн-система и auth, изолированные стейт и стили. Часто монорепо лучше.

words.w: How do you design the API layer of a frontend app?
words.t: Типизированный клиент из OpenAPI/GraphQL, перехватчики auth/ошибок, сверху query-слой с фабриками ключей, мапперы в модели фронта; MSW на том же контракте.
a: How do you design the API layer of a frontend app
words.ex: I generate types and a client from the schema, so when the backend changes the contract, the build fails instead of the user. One place handles the base URL, token refresh, error normalization and tracing headers. On top of it I use TanStack Query with a key factory per entity. If the backend shapes are not convenient, a small mapper converts them to frontend models, so a backend rename touches one file. Mock Service Worker uses the same contract for tests and local development.
words.exT: Типизированный клиент из OpenAPI/GraphQL, перехватчики auth/ошибок, сверху query-слой с фабриками ключей, мапперы в модели фронта; MSW на том же контракте.

words.w: How do you handle errors and loading states consistently across the app?
words.t: Классификация ошибок → свой UI для каждой (reauth, права, поля формы, retry, fallback). Boundaries по регионам, скелетоны с размерами, неожиданное — в мониторинг с контекстом.
a: How do you handle errors and loading states consistently across the app
words.ex: I define an error model early. A 401 means re-login. A 403 shows a permission screen. Validation errors go to the form fields. Network errors offer a retry. Unknown errors show a friendly message and go to monitoring with context. Error boundaries wrap independent parts of the page, so one broken widget does not kill the whole page. For loading I use skeletons with reserved size, so nothing jumps, and I load data at the route level to avoid a chain of spinners.
words.exT: Классификация ошибок → свой UI для каждой (reauth, права, поля формы, retry, fallback). Boundaries по регионам, скелетоны с размерами, неожиданное — в мониторинг с контекстом.

words.w: How do you ship risky UI changes safely?
words.t: Фича-флаги с постепенным раскатом и kill switch, канарейки, мониторинг ошибок и Web Vitals по релизу, A/B с метрикой; флаги удалять после раскатки.
a: How do you ship risky UI changes safely
words.ex: A flag service decides per user or per percentage, so I can deploy the code dark and turn it on first for the team. I watch the error rate, INP and conversion split by the flag. The kill switch turns the feature off without a deploy. Source maps are uploaded, so monitoring points to real code. Every flag has an owner and a removal date; otherwise the code fills with dead branches.
words.exT: Фича-флаги с постепенным раскатом и kill switch, канарейки, мониторинг ошибок и Web Vitals по релизу, A/B с метрикой; флаги удалять после раскатки.

words.w: How do you build design-system components that are accessible, themeable and hard to misuse?
words.t: Headless-примитивы для поведения и a11y, токены в CSS-переменных, типизированные варианты, композиция вместо кучи boolean-пропсов, Storybook + визуальные тесты.
a: How do you build design-system components that are accessible, themeable and hard to misuse
words.ex: I do not write keyboard and ARIA logic for a dropdown myself; I take a headless library and add styles. Colors, spacing and fonts are CSS variables, so a theme switch does not re-render anything. Variants are typed, so size="xl" fails at compile time if it does not exist. Instead of props like isPrimary, isLarge and isIcon, I use slots and children. Storybook with interaction tests and visual snapshots catches regressions, and the stories are the documentation for designers.
words.exT: Headless-примитивы для поведения и a11y, токены в CSS-переменных, типизированные варианты, композиция вместо кучи boolean-пропсов, Storybook + визуальные тесты.

words.w: What breaks when you add a second language late?
words.t: Ломаются склейка строк, множественное число, форматы дат/чисел, длина текста, RTL, сортировка. ICU, Intl.*, логический CSS, вынос строк с первого дня.
a: What breaks when you add a second language late
words.ex: Late internationalization is expensive. Strings are everywhere, and sentences are built by gluing parts, which breaks word order in other languages. ICU MessageFormat handles plurals and gender. Intl.DateTimeFormat, Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat format values per locale. Intl.Collator sorts correctly. Layouts must survive German text that is 30 percent longer, and RTL mirroring through logical properties. Locale files are loaded lazily, so the main bundle stays small.
words.exT: Ломаются склейка строк, множественное число, форматы дат/чисел, длина текста, RTL, сортировка. ICU, Intl.*, логический CSS, вынос строк с первого дня.

words.w: How do you add a Content Security Policy to a React app without breaking it?
words.t: Сначала Report-Only; nonce/hash вместо unsafe-inline, strict-dynamic для чанков; connect-src и frame-ancestors; потом enforce.
a: How do you add a Content Security Policy to a React app without breaking it
words.ex: A strict CSP blocks inline scripts, so most XSS payloads do not run even if an injection happens. The server generates a nonce for each request and puts it on the script tags. strict-dynamic allows scripts that are loaded by a trusted script, which is how bundler chunks work. connect-src limits where fetch can send data. frame-ancestors replaces X-Frame-Options and stops clickjacking. I start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only and a report endpoint, see what would break, fix it, and only then enforce.
words.exT: Сначала Report-Only; nonce/hash вместо unsafe-inline, strict-dynamic для чанков; connect-src и frame-ancestors; потом enforce.

words.w: Where do you store access and refresh tokens in the browser, and why?
words.t: Refresh — в HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie, access — в памяти, не в localStorage; лучше BFF: у браузера только сессионная кука, токены на сервере.
a: Where do you store access and refresh tokens in the browser, and why
words.ex: Any script that gets injected can read localStorage, so a token there means account takeover. I keep the short-lived access token in a JavaScript variable, which limits the damage. The refresh token goes into an HttpOnly cookie, so JavaScript cannot read it; the refresh endpoint then needs CSRF protection. The cleanest option is a BFF: the browser has only a session cookie, and the server holds the OAuth tokens and calls the APIs.
words.exT: Refresh — в HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie, access — в памяти, не в localStorage; лучше BFF: у браузера только сессионная кука, токены на сервере.

words.w: How do you protect a frontend from a malicious npm package?
words.t: Lock-файл и npm ci, аудит и сканеры, минимум зависимостей, ignore-scripts в CI, читать changelog; для CDN — SRI и CSP.
a: How do you protect a frontend from a malicious npm package
words.ex: Most attacks come through transitive dependencies or a stolen maintainer account. I commit the lock file and install with npm ci, so CI gets exactly what I reviewed. I run npm audit and a scanner like Socket that flags install scripts and network access in packages. I update in batches and read changelogs. In CI I install with --ignore-scripts, which blocks the most common payload. For scripts from a CDN I use Subresource Integrity and a CSP. And I keep the number of dependencies small from the start.
words.exT: Lock-файл и npm ci, аудит и сканеры, минимум зависимостей, ignore-scripts в CI, читать changelog; для CDN — SRI и CSP.

words.w: Clickjacking, open redirects and tabnabbing — what are they, and how do you prevent them?
words.t: Фрейминг — frame-ancestors; редирект по ?next — только относительные пути из allowlist; target=_blank — rel=noopener.
a: Clickjacking, open redirects and tabnabbing — what are they, and how do you prevent them
words.ex: In clickjacking an attacker puts my site into an invisible iframe and makes the user click on it. I forbid framing with the CSP frame-ancestors directive. In an open redirect, the login page sends the user to whatever is in ?returnTo, so an attacker can send users to a phishing site. I accept only relative paths from an allowlist. In tabnabbing, a page opened with target=_blank gets window.opener and can change my page. Modern browsers add noopener by default, but I still set rel="noopener" explicitly.
words.exT: Фрейминг — frame-ancestors; редирект по ?next — только относительные пути из allowlist; target=_blank — rel=noopener.

words.w: How do you render user HTML or markdown safely in React?
words.t: Без dangerouslySetInnerHTML для чужого HTML; DOMPurify с allowlist (и на сервере), markdown — через AST в компоненты, проверка схем ссылок; плюс CSP и Trusted Types.
a: How do you render user HTML or markdown safely in React
words.ex: React escapes text by default, so XSS enters through dangerouslySetInnerHTML, through links with a javascript: URL, or through third-party widgets. For user HTML I run DOMPurify with a strict allowlist, on the client and ideally also on the server, and I force rel and target on links. For markdown I parse it into an AST and render my own components, which gives both safety and control. CSP and Trusted Types add another layer of protection.
words.exT: Без dangerouslySetInnerHTML для чужого HTML; DOMPurify с allowlist (и на сервере), markdown — через AST в компоненты, проверка схем ссылок; плюс CSP и Trusted Types.

words.w: What do you test at each level of the frontend testing trophy?
words.t: Статика (TS, lint) → unit для чистой логики → интеграционные с Testing Library и MSW как основной слой → немного E2E на критичные пути. Снэпшоты разметки — нет.
a: What do you test at each level of the frontend testing trophy
words.ex: Types and lint are the cheapest layer and catch a surprising number of bugs. Unit tests cover reducers, utils and complex hooks. Most of my tests are integration tests: I render a feature with a real store and router, mock the network with MSW, and check what the user sees. E2E tests run the important flows, like login and checkout, against a real build; they are slow and sometimes flaky, so there are only a few. I avoid snapshot tests of markup: they fail on every change and prove nothing.
words.exT: Статика (TS, lint) → unit для чистой логики → интеграционные с Testing Library и MSW как основной слой → немного E2E на критичные пути. Снэпшоты разметки — нет.

words.w: How do you test a custom hook and a component that loads data?
words.t: renderHook с wrapper провайдеров; компоненты с данными — MSW с реалистичными ответами, свежий QueryClient без ретраев, findBy/waitFor, ветки loading/success/error.
a: How do you test a custom hook and a component that loads data
words.ex: For a hook I use renderHook and a wrapper with the providers it needs, then I call the returned functions inside act and check the result. For a data component I start an MSW server with handlers for the endpoints, render the component with a fresh QueryClient with retries off, and use findByText to wait for the loaded state. The error case comes from a handler that returns 500. These tests survive a change from fetch to axios or to a generated client, because they test behaviour, not implementation.
words.exT: renderHook с wrapper провайдеров; компоненты с данными — MSW с реалистичными ответами, свежий QueryClient без ретраев, findBy/waitFor, ветки loading/success/error.

words.w: Why are E2E tests flaky, and how do you make them stable?
words.t: Флаки — скрытые гонки: ждать по локаторам, отдельные данные на тест, мок внешних сервисов, выключить анимации, ретраи только как сигнал, трейсы на падении.
a: Why are E2E tests flaky, and how do you make them stable
words.ex: Flakiness is almost always a hidden race. A test checks the text before the UI has finished, or two tests use the same user, or a third-party service is slow. Playwright locators wait automatically, so I never use fixed sleeps. Each test creates its own data through an API or a fixture and cleans up after itself. I mock external services and freeze time when needed. Retries hide problems, so I track flaky tests and fix them. Traces and videos on failure make CI problems easy to debug.
words.exT: Флаки — скрытые гонки: ждать по локаторам, отдельные данные на тест, мок внешних сервисов, выключить анимации, ретраи только как сигнал, трейсы на падении.

words.w: How do you test accessibility, and what cannot be automated?
words.t: axe в unit и E2E ловит треть проблем автоматически; клавиатура, порядок фокуса, объявления скринридера — только руками. Запросы по role в тестах держат a11y.
a: How do you test accessibility, and what cannot be automated
words.ex: Automated checks with jest-axe or the Playwright axe plugin find structural problems and can fail the build. That is cheap, so I always do it. But most real barriers are about flow: can I fill the form with Tab and Enter, does the focus move into the modal and come back after it closes, does the screen reader announce the result. I test the critical flows with the keyboard only and with VoiceOver or NVDA. In unit tests I query by role, which keeps components accessible as a side effect.
words.exT: axe в unit и E2E ловит треть проблем автоматически; клавиатура, порядок фокуса, объявления скринридера — только руками. Запросы по role в тестах держат a11y.

words.w: The app gets slower the longer the tab stays open. How do you investigate?
words.t: Похоже на утечку: график памяти, heap snapshots до/после повторяемого действия, retainers; подписки без cleanup, кэш без gcTime, бесконечно растущий стор.
a: app gets slower the longer the tab stays open. How do you investigate?
The app gets slower the longer the tab stays open. How do you investigate
app gets slower the longer the tab stays open. How do you investigate
words.ex: I use the app for a while and watch the memory graph in the Performance monitor. If it goes up in steps and does not come down after garbage collection, it is a leak. I take a heap snapshot, repeat one action several times, take another snapshot, and compare: which objects grew and who holds them. Common causes in React: subscriptions without cleanup, a query cache with infinite gcTime, a Redux list that keeps every page, and third-party widgets that keep removed DOM nodes. Then I add a test or a memory budget in CI.
words.exT: Похоже на утечку: график памяти, heap snapshots до/после повторяемого действия, retainers; подписки без cleanup, кэш без gcTime, бесконечно растущий стор.

words.w: A search box sends a request on every key press and sometimes shows results for an old query. Fix it properly.
words.t: Debounce, отмена предыдущего запроса (AbortController или ключ запроса), игнорировать несовпадающие ответы, keepPreviousData/useDeferredValue против мигания.
a: search box sends a request on every key press and sometimes shows results for an old query. Fix it properly.
A search box sends a request on every key press and sometimes shows results for an old query. Fix it properly
search box sends a request on every key press and sometimes shows results for an old query. Fix it properly
words.ex: There are three problems here: too many requests, responses in the wrong order, and a flickering UI. A debounce of 200 to 300 milliseconds cuts the requests. Cancelling the previous request in the effect cleanup, or using a query keyed by the search text, guarantees that only the latest result is shown. keepPreviousData or useDeferredValue keeps the old results on screen while the new ones load. I also handle the empty query and a minimum length.
words.exT: Debounce, отмена предыдущего запроса (AbortController или ключ запроса), игнорировать несовпадающие ответы, keepPreviousData/useDeferredValue против мигания.

words.w: Design a reusable Autocomplete component. What do you think about beyond the happy path?
words.t: ARIA combobox и клавиатура, асинхронная загрузка с debounce и отменой, controlled/uncontrolled, дженерик по типу элемента, портал, виртуализация, состояния loading/empty/error.
a: Design a reusable Autocomplete component. What do you think about beyond the happy path
words.ex: I start from the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: the right roles, aria-activedescendant, arrow keys, Escape and Enter. The API takes an async loader that receives an AbortSignal, and a debounce option. It supports both controlled and uncontrolled value. Items are rendered through a render prop, so the component is generic over the item type. The list renders in a portal, so overflow and stacking contexts do not hide it, and it virtualizes when long. It shows loading, empty and error states. Tests cover the keyboard flows and race conditions.
words.exT: ARIA combobox и клавиатура, асинхронная загрузка с debounce и отменой, controlled/uncontrolled, дженерик по типу элемента, портал, виртуализация, состояния loading/empty/error.

words.w: Design a dashboard that shows live data for thousands of users. What is your architecture?
words.t: Push через SSE/WebSocket в нормализованный стор, батчить обновления по кадру, селекторы, виртуализация/canvas, пауза в скрытой вкладке, периодический полный снимок, reconnect с backoff.
a: Design a dashboard that shows live data for thousands of users. What is your architecture
words.ex: Updates can arrive faster than React can render, so I collect them in a buffer and apply them once per frame with a single state update. The store is normalized by id, so one update changes one row, and components subscribe with selectors. Tables and charts are virtualized or drawn on canvas. When the tab is hidden, I stop rendering and let the buffer collapse to the latest values. A periodic full snapshot from the server repairs any missed events, and the connection reconnects with backoff.
words.exT: Push через SSE/WebSocket в нормализованный стор, батчить обновления по кадру, селекторы, виртуализация/canvas, пауза в скрытой вкладке, периодический полный снимок, reconnect с backoff.

words.w: How do you plan a migration from class components to hooks and TypeScript in a large codebase?
words.t: Пошагово: TS с allowJs и мягкими флагами, ужесточать по папкам; конвертировать с листовых компонентов, кодмоды, тесты до рефакторинга, без big-bang.
a: How do you plan a migration from class components to hooks and TypeScript in a large codebase
words.ex: The app must stay shippable all the time. TypeScript goes in with allowJs and strict off, then I turn on strict flags folder by folder. Class components are converted when someone touches them or by risk, starting from the leaves, because they have fewer dependencies. Codemods handle imports and simple patterns. Testing Library tests written before the conversion protect the behaviour. A simple progress dashboard shows the team that the migration moves and has an end date.
words.exT: Пошагово: TS с allowJs и мягкими флагами, ужесточать по папкам; конвертировать с листовых компонентов, кодмоды, тесты до рефакторинга, без big-bang.

words.w: How do you approach a live-coding task in an interview?
words.t: Уточнить требования и крайние случаи, озвучить план и сложность, написать рабочую версию, прогнать примеры вслух, затем рефакторинг и trade-offs, что добавил бы в продакшене.
a: How do you approach a live-coding task in an interview
words.ex: I repeat the task in my own words and ask about inputs, size of data and edge cases. Then I say my plan and its complexity before I type. I write the simplest correct version first. I run it in my head with two or three examples, including an empty input. Only then I improve names and structure. All the time I say what I am doing and why. At the end I say what I would add for production: tests, error handling, accessibility, performance.
words.exT: Уточнить требования и крайние случаи, озвучить план и сложность, написать рабочую версию, прогнать примеры вслух, затем рефакторинг и trade-offs, что добавил бы в продакшене.

words.w: Which data structure gives O(1) lookups in JavaScript, and when do you pick Map over an object?
words.t: Map/Set — O(1) в среднем; Map вместо объекта, когда ключи не строки, важен порядок, много вставок/удалений или ключи от пользователя (нет __proto__).
a: Which data structure gives O(1) lookups in JavaScript, and when do you pick Map over an object
words.ex: A plain object also works as a hash map, but keys become strings, integer-like keys are ordered specially, and a user key like __proto__ is dangerous. A Map keeps any key type, remembers insertion order, has a size property and is faster with many inserts and deletes. A Set is for removing duplicates and for membership checks. Many interview tasks, like two sum, grouping anagrams or counting, are one Map away.
words.exT: Map/Set — O(1) в среднем; Map вместо объекта, когда ключи не строки, важен порядок, много вставок/удалений или ключи от пользователя (нет __proto__).

words.w: Two pointers and sliding window — when do you use them?
words.t: Два указателя — отсортированные массивы и пары; скользящее окно — непрерывные подстроки/подмассивы с состоянием, O(n²) → O(n).
a: Two pointers and sliding window — when do you use them
words.ex: If the input is sorted, two pointers find a pair with a target sum or merge two sequences in linear time. For "longest substring without repeated characters" or "maximum sum of k neighbours", I keep a left and a right index and a Map of counts, and I move the window instead of recomputing the range. The hint is the word "contiguous" or "subarray". Then I think about a window before I write nested loops.
words.exT: Два указателя — отсортированные массивы и пары; скользящее окно — непрерывные подстроки/подмассивы с состоянием, O(n²) → O(n).

words.w: How do you walk a tree like the DOM, and what is the difference between BFS and DFS?
words.t: DFS — вглубь (рекурсия или стек), для подзадач по поддереву; BFS — по уровням через очередь, ближайшее совпадение. Глубокие деревья — явный стек вместо рекурсии.
a: How do you walk a tree like the DOM, and what is the difference between BFS and DFS
words.ex: Recursive DFS is how React renders a tree. I use it to flatten a tree, to search a subtree or to compute depth. Deep trees can overflow the call stack, so a version with an explicit stack is safer. BFS uses a queue and visits the nearest nodes first, which answers questions like "the closest element with this class" or level-order rendering. For the real DOM there is TreeWalker, but on a whiteboard I write the loop myself.
words.exT: DFS — вглубь (рекурсия или стек), для подзадач по поддереву; BFS — по уровням через очередь, ближайшее совпадение. Глубокие деревья — явный стек вместо рекурсии.

words.w: Explain memoization vs dynamic programming with a frontend example.
words.t: Мемоизация — кэш результатов сверху вниз; DP — таблица снизу вверх, без глубокой рекурсии. Примеры: fuzzy-поиск (edit distance), диффы списков.
a: Explain memoization vs dynamic programming with a frontend example
words.ex: Memoization is what useMemo and reselect do: cache by input and reuse. In algorithms it turns an exponential recursion, like Fibonacci or edit distance, into polynomial time. Dynamic programming is the same idea written as a loop over a table. It avoids deep recursion and often needs only one row of memory. Fuzzy matching in a command palette and diffing two lists are everyday places where this matters.
words.exT: Мемоизация — кэш результатов сверху вниз; DP — таблица снизу вверх, без глубокой рекурсии. Примеры: fuzzy-поиск (edit distance), диффы списков.

words.w: How do you implement an LRU cache, and where would you use it in a frontend?
words.t: Map хранит порядок вставки: get — удалить и вставить снова, set сверх лимита — удалить первый ключ, O(1). Для ограниченных кэшей результатов поиска, картинок.
a: How do you implement an LRU cache, and where would you use it in a frontend
words.ex: A JavaScript Map remembers the order of insertion. To mark a key as recently used, I delete it and set it again, so it moves to the end. The oldest key is map.keys().next().value. This gives a clean O(1) LRU cache in about fifteen lines, and it is a common live-coding task. In real life I use it to limit a client cache of search results, parsed documents or thumbnails, so memory does not grow forever.
words.exT: Map хранит порядок вставки: get — удалить и вставить снова, set сверх лимита — удалить первый ключ, O(1). Для ограниченных кэшей результатов поиска, картинок.

words.w: What is the complexity of common array methods, and how do you avoid accidental O(n²) in React code?
words.t: find внутри map, сортировка в рендере, unshift в цикле — скрытое O(n²). Строить Map/индекс один раз через useMemo и называть сложности вслух.
a: What is the complexity of common array methods, and how do you avoid accidental O(n²) in React code
words.ex: If a list renders rows and each row calls users.find(u => u.id === row.userId), that is O(n·m) on every render. A Map built once with useMemo makes it O(n). Sorting or filtering inside render without useMemo repeats O(n log n) work on every key press. unshift and splice at the start are O(n), so building an array by adding to the front in a loop is quadratic. I say these complexities out loud while coding, so the interviewer sees that I think about scale.
words.exT: find внутри map, сортировка в рендере, unshift в цикле — скрытое O(n²). Строить Map/индекс один раз через useMemo и называть сложности вслух.
